english.title: Fail to surrender tachograph card used without authority / falsified / applied for with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being in possession of a tachograph card, namely a

(A)_[company card,]_
(B)_[control card.]_
(C)_[driver card.]_
(D)_[workshop card.]_

(E)_[on which the person using the card was not identified as the holder,]_
(F)_[which had been falsified,]_
(G)_[which had been issued in consequence of an application which included a false statement or forged or altered document,]_

failed to surrender that card to the Secretary of State, by such means and to such address as specified by the Secretary of State, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MEANS AND THE ADDRESS..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 7(1), (4) and (5) of the Passenger and Goods Vehicles (Recording Equipment) (Tachograph Card) Regulations 2006.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
